I built EmbodiWeave to answer two questions.
Which robot checkpoint should I retrain, and
is the result safe to ship?
FalkorDB connects policies, training runs, trials, evaluations,
failures, and decisions. The links preserve what
produced what.
First, the agent queries failed validation suites,
matching the exact artifact hash. A lookalike
checkpoint cannot substitute for measured evidence.
Matching tensor shapes are not enough. FalkorDB
links sensor and action contracts, so incompatible
starting points are excluded.
The planner ranks eligible origins by failed
suites and deficits. Before training, its decision
records the Cypher, parameters, and returned evidence
in FalkorDB.
If FalkorDB is unavailable, planning stops. There
is no silent fallback.
Longer training came first. A retained task
failure then led to rehearsal across training
families. Each attempt added about 300,000 PPO
steps.
FalkorDB chose the rehearsal checkpoint for 600,000
more PPO steps with double the collision
penalty. The saved candidate passed all four
unchanged validation suites.
I froze its hash before a fresh
confirmation batch. All four suites passed. Target
collisions eight in one hundred. The limit
stayed 10%. The earlier failure remains visible.
Physics still exposed a gap. The same
checkpoint, without retraining in MuJoCo, collided six
times in 40 target episodes, and four
times in crossing. This is no physical
safety certificate.
The graph and checksummed evidence make these
results inspectable. EmbodiWeave. Built on FalkorDB.
